predecessors.name: Shaybanids
predecessors.text: Khwarazm, where 'in 1511 his garrison was expelled and power passed to Ilbars'

successors.name: Khorezm People's Soviet Republic
successors.text: the Khiva oasis: Khorezm and the Tashauz (Dashoguz) bank of the Amu Darya delta

ledger.x: 1511: Ilbars expels the Safavid garrison and founds the Arabshahid state at Urgench.
1521: the Amu Darya delta and the Aral shore enter Cliopatria's shape.
1538: Ubaydullah Khan of Bukhara enters Khwarazm.
1538-39: Din Muhammad drives the Bukharans out; Ubaydullah dies in 1539.
1593-94: Abdullah Khan II of Bukhara occupies Khwarazm.
1598: Abdullah Khan II dies and the Bukharan hold lapses.
1599: the capital moves from Konye-Urgench to Khiva.
1740: Nader Shah conquers Khiva.
1747: Nader Shah is murdered and Khiva is free: 'Oman and the Uzbek khanates of Bukhara and Khiva regained independence'.
1748: the Kyzylkum fringe north-west of Bukhara enters Khiva's shape.
1748: the northern Karakum steppe enters Khiva's shape; no opened page dates it.
1791: the Turkmen coast and the Ustyurt/Aral steppe enter Khiva's shape - 1,385 cells to 46.3 N and the Caspian.
1804: the Qongrat dynasty is formalized under Iltuzar Khan.
1811: Muhammad Rahim Khan I recovers the delta.
1812-1813: the lower Syr Darya Kazakhs are subdued ('He subdued the Kazakh tribes of the lower Syr Darya').
1823: Merv comes to Khiva.

c. 1856: the Tekke Turkmen take Merv. 'The Tekke Turkmen became the sovereign power in the area and held it until the Russians occupied the oasis in 1884'; Khiva's 'long Turkmen rebellion (1855-1867)'.
1864: the Caspian Turkmen coast and the Ustyurt/Aral steppe leave Cliopatria's shape (1,579 cells).
11 March 1873: the Russian columns set out.
14 June 1873: Khiva falls.
24 August 1873 (12 August old style): Khiva cedes the Amu Darya Division and becomes a Russian protectorate.
October 1873: a strip of Khivan territory went to Bukhara as a reward for the Amir's neutrality.
2 February 1920: the last khan abdicates and the Khorezm People's Soviet Republic follows.

wars.name: Bukharan wars against Khwarazm
wars.outcome: Ubaydullah Khan kills the khan Avanish in 1538 and is driven out; the Khiva page dates Bukharan wars to '1538-40'.

wars.name: Abdullah Khan II's conquest of Khwarazm
wars.outcome: The sultans of Khiva are captured and executed; the Bukharan hold lapses after 1598.

wars.name: Bekovich-Cherkassky expedition
wars.outcome: The Russian expedition 'attacked Khiva and was soundly defeated', only a few men escaping.

wars.name: Nader Shah's conquest of Khiva
wars.outcome: Nader conquers Khiva, beheads Ilbars and frees 12,000-20,000 slaves; Khiva is an Afsharid vassal or occupied territory until 1746/47.

wars.name: Russian expedition against Khiva (Perovsky)
wars.outcome: 10 October 1839 to June 1840: the Russian column of 5,000 retreats on 13 February 1840 after losing 1,054 men; the aim was a loyal Kazakh khan, not annexation.

wars.name: Turkmen rebellion against Khiva
wars.outcome: 'A long Turkmen rebellion (1855-1867)'; Merv is lost about 1856.

wars.name: Khivan campaign of 1873
wars.outcome: Russian columns converge on Khiva (11 March - 14 June 1873); the khan surrenders on 9-10 June and is reinstated on 14 June; a treaty of 24 August 1873 makes Khiva a protectorate, abolishes slavery, opens the Oxus to Russian boats and sets an indemnity of…

certainty.note: Oasis frontiers against Turkmen and Kazakh nomads and the Karakum; Cliopatria's large 1791-1863 shapes are claimed spheres, not administered land.
The August 1873 treaty ceded the Amu Darya Division, but no opened page gives the line; the remaining frontier is the oasis edge and the Amu Darya.
